title: Agile maturity: growth mindset, training, coaching and servant leadership
blurb: Recall agile maturity as a transformation success factor and tell apart the four concepts that raise it.
question: A team leader makes sure every team member is supported and has what they need, putting the team's needs above their own. Which concept is this?

teach.body: Agile maturity is one of the three success factors of agile transformations named in the syllabus, alongside psychological safety and agile sustainability. Put simply, it is how far people and teams have developed in thinking and working the agile way. It is also one of the key metrics for agility, so PRINCE2 Agile measures it rather than assuming it: agile maturity assessments start in starting up or initiating a project.

teach.h: Four concepts that raise agile maturity
Growth mindset and training and coaching
teach.body: The growth mindset is the fundamental belief that any person can learn, adapt to change and grow; it is often seen as the core of the agile mindset. Training and coaching means people must do more than be informed: they need to understand how to apply the changes, through theoretical training and practical coaching on the job. Informing people and letting them fend for themselves can make all the earlier communication about the change ineffective.

teach.h: From hearing about change to working that way

teach.body: Training plus coaching combats frustration, which the book calls one of the leading causes of demotivation and resistance to change. PRINCE2 Agile suggests a training and coaching plan, ideally mapped to the different needs at each stage of the agile change. As many people as possible should understand what is changing and why, because that leads to smoother adoption across the organization.

Servant leadership, a style associated with Robert Greenleaf, holds that the best way to lead a team is to serve it. The leader puts team members' needs above their own and makes sure everyone is supported, well and has what they need. Rich communication means conveying not just words but emotions, body language, visuals and graphics or icons. The aim is to share as much as possible and avoid misinterpretation, because short agile iterations leave no time for misunderstandings.

teach.h: Maturity is assessed and raised in a loop

teach.body: Corran Logistics has just started agile on its warehouse system project. New agile coach Bethan Morgan is asked to 'roll out the agile tool'. She first runs short training sessions for the whole project team, then coaches each team in its own iterations, using its real backlog. Team lead Kwame Asante shifts to servant leadership, clearing obstacles rather than assigning tasks. Varying maturity across members is discussed openly in retrospectives, not escalated to the board.

teach.text: These four concepts are classic distractors for each other. Leader serving the team: servant leadership. Belief that anyone can grow: growth mindset. Theory plus on-the-job coaching: training and coaching. Emotions, body language and visuals as well as words: rich communication.

items: Agile maturity is a success factor and a key metric; assessments start in starting up or initiating.
Growth mindset: anyone can learn, adapt and grow; often seen as the core of the agile mindset.
Training and coaching: theoretical training plus practical coaching on the job; combats frustration.
A training and coaching plan is ideally mapped to the stages of the agile change.
Servant leadership (Greenleaf): lead by serving, putting team members' needs first.
Rich communication: words plus emotions, body language and visuals; no time for misunderstandings.

summary: You can now recall agile maturity as a success factor of agile transformations and a key metric assessed from starting up or initiating a project. You can also distinguish growth mindset, training and coaching, servant leadership and rich communication as the concepts that raise it.

A.q: Which concept describes a leader who puts team members' needs above their own and makes sure they have what they need?
options: Growth mindset
Rich communication
Training and coaching
Servant leadership
A.why: Servant leadership holds that the best way to lead a team is to serve it, putting members' needs above the leader's own (2.7.3).

whyNot.0: The growth mindset is the belief that any person can learn, adapt and grow.
whyNot.1: Rich communication is about conveying emotions, body language and visuals as well as words.
whyNot.2: Training and coaching is about theory plus practical coaching on the job.

A.q: In PRINCE2 Agile, what does 'rich communication' refer to?
options: Communicating words plus emotions, body language and visuals
Sending detailed written reports to all stakeholders
Holding a formal meeting at every stage boundary
Using one approved formal channel for all project messages
A.why: Rich communication means communicating not just words but also emotions, body language, visuals and graphics or icons (2.7.3).

whyNot.1: Written reports are text only; rich communication goes beyond words.
whyNot.2: Stage boundary meetings are governance events, not the meaning of rich communication.
whyNot.3: Restricting channels is not what rich communication describes.

A.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, what does the 'training and coaching' concept involve?
options: Informing people of the change by email
Theoretical training plus practical coaching on the job
Coaching senior managers so that they can cascade it to teams
Self-study courses that people complete alone
A.why: People need to understand how to apply the changes through theoretical training and practical coaching on the job (2.7.3).

whyNot.0: Informing people alone, leaving them to fend for themselves, can make communication about the change ineffective.
whyNot.2: The book stresses that as many people as possible should understand the change, not just managers.
whyNot.3: Self-study lacks the practical, on-the-job coaching element.

B.q: Why does PRINCE2 Agile say training and coaching are important during an agile change?
options: They cut the cost of agile tools
They remove the need for a separate team coach role
They combat frustration that fuels resistance
They let the board skip progress reviews
B.why: Training plus coaching combats frustration, one of the leading causes of demotivation and resistance to change (2.7.3).

whyNot.0: Tool costs are not the reason the book gives.
whyNot.1: Coaching is delivered by coaches; it does not remove the team coach role.
whyNot.3: Progress reviews are unaffected; training does not replace governance.

B.q: Why does PRINCE2 Agile place emphasis on rich communication?
options: Long documents are needed for audit
Short iterations leave no time for misunderstandings
Supplier contracts require formal written notices of change
Remote teams cannot hold live meetings
B.why: Rich communication shares as much information as possible to minimize misinterpretation, because short iterations leave no time for misunderstandings (2.7.3).

whyNot.0: Rich communication is not about long documents; it goes beyond text.
whyNot.2: Written contract notices are text only, the opposite of rich communication, and are not the reason given.
whyNot.3: Remote teams can and should hold live meetings; that is not the reason given.

B.q: When are agile maturity assessments first carried out, according to PRINCE2 Agile?
options: During closing a project
During managing a stage boundary
During controlling a stage, after authorization
During starting up or initiating a project
B.why: Agile maturity assessments are initially carried out during starting up a project or initiating a project (12.4.1).

whyNot.0: Closing reviews lessons and trends; it is not when maturity is first assessed.
whyNot.1: Stage boundaries come later; the initial assessment is in starting up or initiating.
whyNot.2: Controlling a stage follows authorization; the first assessment is earlier.

C.q:
Which two statements about raising agile maturity are correct?
1. A training and coaching plan is ideally mapped to the stages of the agile change.
2. Informing people about the change is enough for it to stick.
3. Servant leaders make sure team members are supported and have what they need.
4. The growth mindset means leaders put their own goals first.
options: 1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4
1 and 3
C.why: The book suggests a training and coaching plan mapped to the stages of the change (1) and describes servant leaders supporting their team (3) (2.7.3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: informing people and leaving them to fend for themselves can make the change ineffective.
whyNot.1: Both are wrong: informing is not enough, and the growth mindset is a belief that anyone can grow.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is wrong: the growth mindset is about people's ability to learn and grow.

C.q: Early in an agile transformation at Pellow Foods, the new agile coach must raise the team's agile maturity. Which approach fits PRINCE2 Agile, and why?
options: Send a briefing email, because informing people is enough
Train managers first, because they will cascade it
Train and coach on real work, because people need both
Introduce a new tool, because tools build agile habits
C.why: People need theoretical training and practical coaching on the job to understand how to apply the change (2.7.3).

whyNot.0: Informing people and letting them fend for themselves can make the change ineffective.
whyNot.1: As many people as possible should understand what is changing and why, not just managers.
whyNot.3: A tool before knowledge and skills skips the training and coaching people need.

C.q: Team members on an agile project show very different levels of agile maturity. How does PRINCE2 Agile suggest this is handled, and under which principle?
options: Transparently with the team, under learn from experience
By escalation to the board, under manage by exception
By replacing members, under define roles and responsibilities
By an issue report, under manage by stages
C.why: Varying levels of agile maturity are handled transparently as lessons are gathered with the team, which supports learn from experience; they are not escalated (Table 5.1).

whyNot.1: Manage by exception applies when tolerances are forecast to be exceeded, not to differing maturity.
whyNot.2: Replacing people is not the suggested response; coaching and learning are.
whyNot.3: Differing maturity is not a formal issue to report under manage by stages.

reteach.title: Learning to drive
reteach.question: How do the four concepts work together?

blocks.body: You believe you can learn to drive (growth mindset). You study the Highway Code and then practise with an instructor on real roads (training and coaching). The instructor's job is to help you, not to show off (servant leadership). And they point, gesture and explain, not just recite rules (rich communication). Agile maturity grows the same way.

blocks.text: Reading the Highway Code alone does not make a driver. Informing people without practical coaching does not make agile stick.

explain.h: A success factor and a metric
explain.body: Agile maturity is one of three success factors of agile transformations and a key metric for agility, first assessed in starting up or initiating (2.7.3, 2.7.6, 12.4.1).

test.q: Which of these is one of the key metrics for agility that agile maturity assessments are based on?
options: Agile maturity
Story point totals
Number of releases
Budget spent per stage
test.why: Agile maturity assessments use the key metrics for agility: psychological safety, agile maturity and agile sustainability (12.4.1).

whyNot.1: Story points estimate work; they are not a key metric for agility.
whyNot.2: Release counts are a planning detail, not a key metric for agility.
whyNot.3: Spend is a cost measure, not one of the key metrics for agility.

explain.body: Theory plus practical coaching on the job; combats frustration; ideally a training and coaching plan mapped to the stages of the change (2.7.3).

test.q: In PRINCE2 Agile, what is a training and coaching plan ideally mapped to?
options: The project's tolerances
The stages of the agile change
The team's Definition of Done
The risk register entries
test.why: The book suggests a training and coaching plan, ideally mapped to the different needs at the stages of an agile change initiative (2.7.3).

whyNot.0: Tolerances relate to managing by exception.
whyNot.2: The DoD sets completion criteria for work.
whyNot.3: The risk register records risks, not learning needs.

explain.body: Associated with Robert Greenleaf: lead a team by serving it, putting members' needs above your own and making sure they have what they need (2.7.3).

explain.caption: The leader supports the team from below.

test.q: Which leadership style does PRINCE2 Agile associate with Robert Greenleaf?
options: Command and control
Servant leadership
Transactional leadership
Growth leadership
test.why: Servant leadership is associated with Robert Greenleaf; the leader serves the team (2.7.3).

whyNot.0: Command and control is the opposite of serving the team.
whyNot.2: Transactional leadership is not the style the book describes.
whyNot.3: Growth mindset is a belief about learning, not a leadership style named after Greenleaf.

explain.body: Communicating words plus emotions, body language, visuals and graphics, to minimize misinterpretation in short iterations (2.7.3).

test.q: A team replaces long email threads with short video calls using a shared whiteboard. Which concept does this reflect?
options: Servant leadership
Growth mindset
Rich communication
Training and coaching
test.why: Adding tone, body language and visuals to words is rich communication (2.7.3).

whyNot.0: Servant leadership is about the leader serving the team.
whyNot.1: Growth mindset is the belief that people can learn and grow.
whyNot.3: Training and coaching is about learning to apply the changes.
